title: Tokyo Was Once Called Edo
visual_style: photographic travel documentary; no characters, no illustration assets
script: Tokyo's story begins with a different name: Edo.
For centuries, Edo grew around the seat of the Tokugawa shogunate, becoming one of Japan's major urban centers.
In 1868, the imperial capital moved from Kyoto to Edo, and the city took the name Tokyo, meaning eastern capital.
That history is still part of the city's landscape: traditional districts, shrines, gardens, and modern streets sit within the same enormous metropolis.
For a history-focused visit, choose one area rather than racing across the whole city. Walk slowly, and look for what has changed around older streets and sacred sites.
Before you go, check current access details for any museum or site you plan to enter.
